541 {3Jο 16, 12 13}3Ἀντὶ τοῦ συνῳδά μοι λαλεῖ· οὐ γὰρ ἐνδεὲς τὸ πνεῦμα·
ἰδιοσύστατον γὰρ ὂν ὡς ὁμοούσιον πατρὸς καὶ υἱοῦ πάντα οἶδε καὶ ἰσχύει ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ
ποιεῖν. 542 {3Jο 16, 13}3Ὅταν τὸ πνεῦμα διδάξῃ ὑμᾶς, τότε δυνήσεσθε τῶν νομικῶν
ἀποστῆναι τύπων καὶ τὴν «ἐν πνεύματι καὶ ἀληθείᾳ» ποιῆσαι λατρείαν.οὐ μεῖζον
τοῦ υἱοῦ τὸ πνεῦμα, φησίν. διὸ οὐδὲν ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ λαλήσει, ἀλλ' ἃ ἀκούει· ἃ γὰρ ἐγώ,
κἀκεῖνος ἐρεῖ.τὸ πνεῦμα διδάξει τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τὰ τῆς τοῦ υἱοῦ θεότητος καὶ δόξης
καὶ τῆς πρὸς τὸν πατέρα ἰσότητος.οὐ δι' ἀσθένειαν οὐ λαλεῖ, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὴν ἀκριβῆ
συμφωνίαν τῆς τριάδος τοῦτο εἶπεν. 543 {3Jο 16, 14}3Ὡς φυσικῶς ἔχων ὁ υἱὸς τὰ τοῦ
πατρὸς διὰ τὸ ὁμοούσιον εἶπεν καὶ τὰ τοῦ πνεύματος ἴδια αὐτοῦ εἶναι ὡς ὄντα κοινὰ
τὰ τῆς τριάδος. 544 {3Jο 16, 16}3Ἵνα μὴ λυπήσῃ τοὺς μαθητάς, καὶ οὐκ εἶπεν, ὅτι
ἀποθνῄσκω, ἀλλ' οὐ θεωρεῖτέ με. 545 {3Jο 16, 18}3Ὑπὸ τῆς λύπης οὐκ ἐνενόουν καὶ
ὅτι μὲν ἀπῄει ᾔδεσαν, πῶς δὲ ἥξει, οὐκ ᾔδεσαν· ἠγνόουν γὰρ τὴν ἀνάστασιν πρὸ τῆς
ἐκβάσεως. 546 {3Jο 16, 19–}3Ἐπειδὴ σφόδρα λυπούμενοι οὐκ ἤθελον ἀκούειν περὶ
τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ, βουλόμενος αὐτοῖς ἐμπῆξαι τὸ δόγμα τοῦτο εἶπεν τὸ κλαύσετε,
μετὰ τὴν λύπην ἔσται χαρά. 547 {3Jο 16, 21}3Μισθὸς τῆς λύπης ἔσται ὑμῶν ἡ χαρὰ ὡς
καὶ τῇ λύπῃ τῆς ὠδινούσης ἡ ἀπὸ τοῦ τοκετοῦ χαρά. ἐπειδὴ <ὅτε> ἀπέθανεν, αὐτοῖς
ἐφαίνετο ἀπὸ λύπης εἰς χαρὰν ἐλθεῖν, τῷ τῆς τικτούσης παραδείγματι κέχρηται. 548
{3Jο 16, 22}3Ἐπειδὴ πεισθήσεσθε, ὅτι ὡς θεὸς ἀνέστην καὶ οὐκέτι ἀποθνῄσκω, κἂν
μετὰ τῆς σαρκὸς ἀναβῶ εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν. 549 {3Jο 16, 25}3Τὸν τῆς ἀναστάσεως
καιρὸν λέγει. 550 {3Jο 16, 25}3Ὡς γὰρ ἐν παροιμίαις λαλεῖ ταῦτα ὁ Χριστὸς ὡς
παρακατιὼν λέγει· οὐ γὰρ δύναται κατὰ τὸ γράμμα νοεῖσθαι. ἐκεῖνος δὲ αἰτεῖ καὶ
λαμβάνει ὁ τὰ λυσιτελῆ αἰτῶν πρὸς βελτίωσιν ψυχαῖς. παροιμίαν λέγει τὸν ἀσαφῆ
καὶ ἐγκε καλυμμένον λόγον. διὰ τὴν νηπιότητα αὐτῶν ἐπεσκιασμένως λέγει. ὅταν δὲ
προκόψητε, τότε ἀποκαλύπτω ὑμῖν τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς δόξαν. μετὰ τὴν ἀνάστασιν
σαφῶς ὑμῖν ἐρῶ τὰ περὶ τοῦ πατρός. ὅταν λάβητε τὸ πνεῦμα, τότε λήψεσθε σαφῆ τὴν
περὶ υἱοῦ καὶ πατρὸς γνῶσιν. 551 {3Jο 16, 26}3∆ύναται μὲν ὡς θεὸς δοῦναι, πλὴν ὡς
ἤδη εἰπὼν τὸ αἰτῶ οἰκονομικῶς ὡς ἄνθρωπος ἐνέμεινεν τῷ λόγῳ. 552 {3Jο 16,
28}3Ἐκ τῆς οὐσίας, φησίν, ἐξῆλθον τοῦ πατρὸς ἀδιαιρέτως ὢν ἐν πατρὶ καὶ
ἰδιοσυστάτως ἔχων ἐν ἐμαυτῷ τὸν πατέρα. οὔτε ὅτε γέγονεν ἄνθρωπος ἀπολειφθεὶς
τοῦ πατρὸς ἐληλυθέναι λέγεται εἰς τὸν κόσμον οὔτε ὅτ' ἀνελήφθη μετὰ τῆς σαρκός,
ἀπελείφθη τοῦ κόσμου· θεὸς γάρ ἐστι πληρῶν τὰ πάντα. 553 {3Jο 16, 32}3Τὸ «ἄρτι
πιστεύετε», ἀνθρωπινώτερον τοῦτο λέγει· καθὸ γὰρ θεὸς
pass_a_gloss: Meaning: the Spirit speaks in tune with me. He is not deficient; self standing and sharing Father and Son substance, he knows all and can act from himself. Once the Spirit teaches, you can leave legal shadows and worship in spirit and truth. The Spirit is not above the Son, so he will not speak from himself but what he hears matching what I say. He will teach the Son's Godhead, glory, and equality with the Father. Silence is not from weakness but from the Trinity's exact accord. Because the Son naturally holds the Father's goods through shared substance, he says the Spirit's goods are his too as Trinity common goods. To spare the disciples grief he said you do not see me rather than I die. Grief blocked understanding: they knew he was leaving but not how he would come, ignorant of rising before it happened. Deeply sad and unwilling to hear of his death, he fixed the teaching with you will weep; joy follows grief. Joy pays grief as childbirth joy pays labor pain. When he died they seemed to move from grief to joy, so he used the birthing woman as figure. You will be sure I rose as God and die no more, even if I ascend with flesh. He means rising time. Christ speaks proverbially for what cannot be taken by the letter. The one who asks useful things for soul betterment receives. Proverb means veiled unclear speech. For their infancy he speaks shaded; when you advance I unveil the Father's glory. After rising I will speak plainly about the Father. Receiving the Spirit brings clear knowledge of Son and Father. As God he can give, yet keeping I ask he stays with the economy word as man. I came from the Father's essence, indivisible in him and holding him self standing in myself. Becoming man did not leave him behind the Father as coming into the world, nor did fleshly ascent leave him behind the world; he is God filling all. Now you believe is said more humanly; as God I am in the Father by nature without gap. Condescension spoke it because disciples wanted to hear it. Christ proved stronger than worldly sin and grants believers victory. Or as man from us he proved stronger than death and corruption and grace crosses to us. So take heart: as man he won and we seem winners in him; a win as God alone would mean nothing for us. Hour is the fitting passion time he chose to suffer, as with the wine saying, not fate without hypostasis. Prayer form trains us in trials to pray and flee to God. Lest hearers stumble, by economy he says what you gave me. Note: right faith is true life granting its goods to believers. He says he was sent not as forced servant of the Father's will
pass_b_english: That is: he speaks in agreement with me; for the Spirit is not lacking; being self-subsistent as consubstantial with Father and Son he knows all things and has power of himself to act.

When the Spirit teaches you, then you will be able to leave the legal types and make the worship “in spirit and truth” (John 4:23–24). The Spirit is not greater than the Son, he says. Therefore he will speak nothing from himself, but what he hears; for what I say, that one also will say. The Spirit will teach human beings the things of the Son’s Godhead and glory and of equality with the Father. He does not fail to speak from weakness; he said this because of the exact harmony of the Trinity.
As the Son naturally has the Father’s things through the consubstantial, he said that the Spirit’s own things are also his, as the things of the Trinity are common.
So as not to grieve the disciples, he also did not say “I die,” but “you do not see me.”
Under grief they did not understand, and that he was departing they knew, but how he would come they did not know; for they were ignorant of the resurrection before the outcome.
Since being deeply grieved they did not want to hear about his death, wanting to fix this doctrine in them he said “you will weep”; after the grief there will be joy.

The reward of your grief will be joy, as also for the woman in labor the joy from childbirth after the grief. Since when he died it appeared to them to pass from grief into joy, he used the example of the woman giving birth.
Since you will be persuaded that as God I rose and die no longer, even if with the flesh I go up into heaven.
He means the time of the resurrection.

For as in proverbs Christ speaks these things as one going on to say; for it cannot be understood according to the letter. And that one asks and receives who asks what is profitable for bettering souls. He calls proverb the unclear and veiled word. Because of their infancy he speaks in a shaded way. But when you advance, then I unveil to you the Father’s glory. After the resurrection I will speak clearly to you the things about the Father. When you receive the Spirit, then you will receive clear knowledge about Son and Father.
He can as God give, yet as already saying “I ask” he stayed with the word by economy as man.

From the essence, he says, I came out from the Father, being indivisibly in the Father and having the Father self-subsistently in myself. Neither when he became man, left behind by the Father, is he said to have come into the world, nor when he was taken up with the flesh was he left behind by the world; for he is God filling all things.
The “now you believe” he says more humanly; for insofar as I am God, I am in God and Father naturally and without interval. He said this by condescension, since the disciples wanted to hear this.

Christ appeared better and more powerful than every worldly sin and also gives the faithful to conquer. Or that Christ, having come to be from us insofar as man, appeared better than death and corruption and the grace passes over to us. And so we ought to take courage that we will receive, since as man he conquered and we seem in him to have conquered; for if as God he conquered, it is nothing toward us.
He calls hour the fitting time of the passion, at which he judged to suffer—as also he said about the wine—not the hypostasis-less fate.
Through the form of prayer he trains us in trials to pray and take refuge in God.
So that the hearers may not take offense, by economy he says “what you have given me.”
It must be noted that right faith is the true life that grants its own goods to those who believe. He says he was sent not as from necessity serving the Father’s will
